clue.text: Sheet which is on offer we hear

indicators.note: says the phrase meaning available to buy is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: goods on offer are for sale, the phrase said aloud here

explanation.surface: A sheet of paper that someone tells us is up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheet' looks like paper or bedding, but in sailing a sheet is also a poetic word for a sail; FOR SALE spoken sounds like the sail at the front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a literary word for a sail, and this one is the sail set on the foremast.

clue.text: Enough beer to upset the family tree?

indicators.note: upset says the order is overturned, so the family word is moved from the front to the back

parts.note: family is kin and a tree is a fir, so the phrase gives those two words in that order

explanation.surface: Drinking so much beer that you knock over the family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family tree' reads as genealogy, but it is two separate words; 'upset' moves the first behind the second. A firkin is a small cask of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A firkin is a small cask, a measure of about nine gallons of ale.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: Talking about people who have died.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell a story is to narrate or recount it in speech.

clue.text: Sergeant Major and soldiers are unctuous

parts.note: an army is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: The sergeant major and his troops are oily and ingratiating.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an oily, ingratiating, fawning manner.

clue.text: Evil to repeat for the un. educated

definitions.note: an adjective for people who cannot read, matching 'the uneducated' used as a description

parts.note: ill can mean evil or harmful, as in ill deeds
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Wickedness recited again and again for those who never went to school.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'un. educated' is a typesetting break in 'uneducated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to read or write has had little schooling.

indicators.note: the word for the plant comes after the metal symbol in the answer, as this placement word directs

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a rush is a reed-like waterside plant

explanation.surface: Someone went along with a plan to hurry once the silver was in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' reads as a verb meaning hurry, but here it is the marsh plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agreed to something is to have given consent, a straight synonym.

explanation.surface: Timber or metal chains joining things.
explanation.definitionFit: Woods and irons are kinds of stick used on the course; links is also an organisation running a seaside course.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a tern is a seabird
a means one

explanation.surface: A one-time bird abandoned out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer or exterior things are on the outside, a synonym.

clue.text: Became gloomy and dared little Kenneth to enter

indicators.note: the short name is put into the word dared, as to enter says

parts.note: taken as written
Ken is the short, little form of the name Kenneth

explanation.surface: The light faded and someone challenged young Kenneth to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: When things darken they grow dim and gloomy.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
liable to do something means likely to do it

explanation.surface: Troops who can probably be counted on to be dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dependable can be counted on, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Racehorse starting powerfully but finishing afterwards

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word powerfully is taken, as starting suggests

parts.note: to finish afterwards is to come in later

explanation.surface: A horse that sets off strongly in a race but comes home well behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A plater is a modest racehorse that runs in selling races, called plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A plater is a low-grade racehorse, one running in plate or selling races.

explanation.surface: A suggestion that something might be near at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint is to suggest something indirectly, a verb sense; close friends are dear and familiar ones, the adjective sense.

clue.text: It's hard to get a hundred in a panic

indicators.note: the letter for a hundred is placed within the word for a panic

parts.note: a scare is a sudden fright or panic
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: In a cricket match, scoring a century is tough when nerves take hold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a nervous batsman trying to score a hundred, a century in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply is difficult to obtain.

clue.text: Record how old we are and dishearten

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
our age is how old we are

explanation.surface: Writing down our ages turns out to be depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to dampen their confidence or spirit.

explanation.surface: Someone eloquent who also has venues for gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: An eloquent speaker expresses things clearly; a jointed body has places where its parts meet and bend.

clue.text: Sailor found the answer and was pardoned

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, an ordinary sailor
to have solved a problem is to have found the answer

explanation.surface: A seaman worked out the puzzle and was let off.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is active in form but the clue reads it as passive: the sins were forgiven.
explanation.definitionFit: To be forgiven a sin or offence is to be set free from blame.

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of ace pilot into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A star flier given a musical arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing is in the manner of verse.

clue.text: Storing up a large amount -in German capital

parts.note: a mass is a large amount
taken as written

indicators.note: the capital letter of a word is its first, so the opening letter of German is taken

explanation.surface: Hoarding a great deal of money in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' looks like Berlin, but it is just the first letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarding up a stock means gathering or accumulating it.

clue.text: Sweepers getting credit for aerial transport

parts.note: brooms are tools that sweep
on tick means on credit, British slang

explanation.surface: Cleaning tools bought on account turn out to be a way of flying.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is informal British for buying on credit; the flying stick is the witch's.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch's flying stick is the classic magical vehicle through the air.

parts.note: tar is an old slang word for a sailor
to get something is to obtain it

explanation.surface: A goal for a seaman to achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal is something you set out to hit.

explanation.surface: Securing a cog on a gear wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To pin someone's arms is to bind them; a small cog that meshes with a larger gear is a small toothed wheel.

clue.text: Alliance giving the French a fever

parts.note: le is French for the
ague is a malarial fever with shivering

explanation.surface: A partnership in which the French get sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A union of nations or clubs is a confederation or alliance.

explanation.surface: Someone slow on the uptake and definitely not sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow person is mentally blunt; an angle wider than ninety degrees is the opposite of a sharp one in geometry.

indicators.note: the word for the clergyman goes round the numeral, as about signals

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A priest who cures, with four people around.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that heals is restorative, the adjective sense of cure.

clue.text: Prey I caught with vigour outside

indicators.note: the word for vigour is placed around the other letters, as outside says

parts.note: vim means energy or vigour
Ct is the column heading for catches in cricket statistics

explanation.surface: A hunter boasts of catching quarry with great energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket statistics tables head the catches column 'Ct', the abbreviation the setter uses for 'caught'; 'outside' puts the energy word around I and that abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that is hunted is the casualty of the hunter, a synonym.

parts.note: a gang is a mob of people
ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A thin crowd heads off on a fishing trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanky, tall and thin person can be described this way.

indicators.note: the sail word is set inside the river name, as in shows

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
a lug, or lugsail, is a four-cornered sail

explanation.surface: Boats sailing on a river that has burst its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A great inundation of water is a synonym for a flood.

explanation.surface: Statements spoken when a verdict is passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit is a string of words; a court's ruling is the punishment passed.
